extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents and counsel in USPTO disciplinary proceedings; OED staff and USPTO officials
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 approving an Affidavit of Resignation and ordering exclusion on consent from practice before the USPTO; it records required acknowledgements, alleged misconduct, the legal consequences for reinstatement, and publication/complying obligations. Useful as the procedural and substantive checklist for approving/processing resignations-with-consent in OED matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to approve affidavit and exclude (statutory/regulatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, the USPTO Director has the authority to approve an Affidavit of Resignation and to exclude a practitioner on consent from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal basis for approving an affidavit of resignation and ordering exclusion; establishes jurisdiction for the Director to effect such exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a) for affidavit approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director must determine that the Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the affidavit meets §11.27(a) requirements, the Director may approve the affidavit and order exclusion on consent; the Final Order records that determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must state consent is freely and voluntarily rendered
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must acknowledge that his consent is freely and voluntarily rendered, and he is not being subjected to coercion or duress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express, uncoerced consent is a threshold requirement for an exclusion on consent under §11.27; absence of such an acknowledgment would undermine approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of OED investigation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.22 and factual background
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must be aware that the OED Director opened an investigation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.22 and that the investigation obtained information including: (a) guilty plea in U.S. v. Gary M Sutter to violating 18 U.S.C. § 2252(a)(2); (b) commitment to custody of the Bureau of Prisons for 72 months; (c) submission of application for retirement or resignation in Ohio pursuant to Ohio Gov. Bar R. VI(11)(B); (d) resignation accepted by the Supreme Court of Ohio as resignation with disciplinary action pending; and (e) withdrawal of rights/privileges to practice law in Ohio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit should recite the salient investigative findings so the respondent knowingly relinquishes practice rights in light of those facts; listing these facts provides the basis for the OED Director's opinion and for consequences on reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director's opinion of violations of USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (§11.804(b),(h),(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is of the opinion that the respondent violated: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b) (professional misconduct for a practitioner to commit a criminal act that reflects adversely on the practitioner's honesty, trustworthiness or fitness); § 11.804(h) (professional misconduct for a practitioner to be publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by any duly constituted authority of a State); and § 11.804(i) (professional misconduct to engage in other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the USPTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit need not contain admissions to these violations, but the OED Director's expressed opinion frames the disciplinary grounds supporting exclusion and informs reinstatement presumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement presumptions under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 (facts and inability to defend)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that, if and when he applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for the purpose of determining the application for reinstatement, that: (a) the facts regarding him in OED File No. — are true; and (b) he could not have successfully defended himself against the allegations embodied in the opinion of the OED Director that he violated 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.804(b), 11.804(h), and 11.804(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a collateral-consequence admission specific to the reinstatement process: the affidavit waives dispute of facts/defenses for reinstatement adjudication purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent must understand and acknowledge relevant USPTO regulations (§§11.5(b),11.24,11.25,11.27,11.58,11.59,11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges he has fully read and understands 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.5(b), 11.24, 11.25, 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60 and is fully aware of the legal and factual consequences of consenting to exclusion from practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit should show informed relinquishment of practice rights by demonstrating knowledge of the cited regulations and their consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order effect: exclusion on consent from practice (scope and commencement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be excluded on consent from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters commencing on the date of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exclusion applies to practice before the USPTO across patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters and takes effect as of the Final Order's date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and notice content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's electronic FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the provided 'Notice of Exclusion on Consent' text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication obligations include specific content (acceptance of affidavit, basis of investigation, OED opinion citations, reinstatement presumptions, and statutory/regulatory citations) and ensure public notice of disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly conditions the respondent on compliance with §11.58 (which concerns [practitioner obligations on resignation/exclusion/publication procedures]); compliance is a continuing obligation during exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any reinstatement application must follow §11.60 procedures; the affidavit's reinstatement presumptions and other conditions will govern the reinstatement process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioners are subject to USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent, as a registered patent attorney, is subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms that disciplinary standards derive from the USPTO professional conduct rules applicable to registered practitioners.
